title_original: ‘The Year of the Ghost,’ About Misogyny in China, Wins Best Film at IDFA Documentary Festival

blocks.text: Louis HotHotHot ‘s “The Year of the Ghost” won best film in the International Competition section of leading documentary festival IDFA on Thursday.
The award is accompanied by a €15,000 ($16,462) cash prize.

The film, a co-production between Netherlands and China, focuses on the director’s mother and sister in China following his father’s death. He explores how misogyny has affected the lives of the women in his family across the generations.

blocks.text: The film was told with “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love,” the jury said. They added that they were “astonished by this work of singular artistic vision exploring deep family dynamics and connections, set against the wider societal forces and gender constraints inherited across generations.”

The award for best directing, and a €5,000 prize, in the International Competition went to Joël Richmond Mathieu Akafou for “Lonan Tché,” a co-production between France, Italy, Ivory Coast and Senegal.

The film is an intimate double portrait of two young men from Ivory Coast who fled to Europe together. Kader now has legal residency in Italy, while Inza is undocumented in France. For both, the gap between expectation and reality proves almost impossible to bridge.

The jury commented, “Through its deeply attaching characters and the subtitle proximity the filmmaker established with them, the film depicts two overgrown kids in their quest for a dream they might never reach, elevating them to almost mythical figures, enduring their human condition.”
The award for best editing in the International Competition went to “The Year of the Ghost,” with editing by HotHotHot and Chris van Oers.
The award for best cinematography in the International Competition went to “Bardi” (Morocco) by Tala Hadid, with cinematography by Hadid.
The special mention for International Competition went to “Hazara Town” by Khadim Dai (Belgium, Australia, Germany).
The jury members of the International Competition were Barbara Orlicz-Szczypuła, Hania Mroué, Katy Léna N’diaye, Laura Poitras and Luuk Bouwman.
The award for best film in the Envision Competition went to Riccardo Giacconi for “Memories of Lightning” (France, Italy). The award is accompanied by a €15,000 cash prize.
The jury said it was a “film that captures the silence of things falling, like distant flashes of lightning that are sure to herald the storm.”

The award for best directing (worth €5,000) in the Envision Competition went to Yuula Benivolski for “The Black Box Is Orange” (Canada). The award for outstanding artistic contribution went to Sibilla Scinti Roger for her work on “Memories of Lightning” (France, Italy).
The special mention for Envision Competition went to “Memories” (Belgium, France) by Anna Falguères.
The jury members of the Envision Competition were Firouzeh Khosrovani, Hélder Beja, Hicham Khalidi, Isabel Pagliai and Jonathan Perel.
The DocLab Award for immersive non-fiction went to Michał Stankiewicz for “Being in You” (Poland). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 cash prize.
The jury said, “Through a tender exploration of life and death, this project invited us to see how VR can be a tool to memorialize while also bringing a sense of embodied presence.”
The special mention for the DocLab Competition for immersive non-fiction went to “Shifting Connections” (Taiwan) by Tungyen Chou.
The jury members of the DocLab Competition for immersive non-fiction were Blake Kammerdiener, Natalie Paneng and Roel Wouters.
Ant Hampton won the DocLab Award for digital storytelling with “All the Downtime” (Netherlands, Belgium). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 cash prize.

“The work invites us to see the increasing entanglements between technocapitalism, precarious labor conditions, automation of human work, disregards of natural ecosystems and the new warlords of corporate fascism,” said the jury.
The special mention for the DocLab Competition for digital storytelling went to “Plum Road Tea Dream” (Belgium) by Samuel Baidoo.
The jury members of the DocLab Competition for digital storytelling were Abel Enklaar, Claudix Vanesix and Pegah Tabassinejad.
The award for best first feature across all sections went to “Hazara Town” by Khadim Dai (Belgium, Australia, Germany). The award is accompanied by a €5,000 prize.
The special mention went to “She Was Not Alone” (Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, U.S.) by Hussein Al-asadi.
The jury members were Gianluca Matarrese, Gugi Gumilang and Ketevan Kipiani.
